samples.text: For now, the period runs on a stopgap: manual agency code mapping override applied to complete valuation for the period. Its basis is a confirmed defect, recorded as stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. Because the fault sits in reference data rather than in the valuation logic, engineers can route around it by hand without changing code. Against the normal path, the override swaps an automatic code lookup for a manual one, valid for this period only. It yields a usable valuation, yet it gives no assurance for the next run and depends on the engineers who applied it. Anyone deciding whether to wait should not expect a permanent repair soon, as none is ready at the time of writing. The working assumption is to use the overridden output for operations and to expect the same manual step next period unless the register entry is corrected first. Legacy and cloud agency codes still sit side by side, and the link between them is still kept by

Established cause: stale legacy-to-new agency code mapping in the reference data register. The inventory valuation service received agency codes that no longer matched a current entry, and the valuation run could not resolve them. That was not the first explanation. Initial triage recorded the cause as overnight ERP outage, a reasonable guess for an overnight batch that stopped without a clear error. Log evidence closed that line of enquiry: ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. With the upstream system cleared, the review moved to reference data and found the stale mapping. Classification of the root cause went one level further: control failure: the mapping table has no registered owner and no required reviewer. A stale row is the symptom, and the missing control over the table is the condition that let the row decay.
